claim_verdicts.evidence: gitglossary(7) head: "A named reference to the commit at the tip of a branch. Heads are stored in a file in $GIT_DIR/refs/heads/ directory". Execution (lab box, build-history.sh): `git reflog show feature/shipping` ends with "09c8526 feature/shipping@{2}: branch: Created from main" - creating a branch also writes a reflog entry, so "stores only the name and id" is too strong. claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A branch is a name that points at one commit. Creating one writes that name and the commit id (plus a one-line log entry of where the name has been); it copies no files, so its cost does not grow with the size of the project.

claim_verdicts.evidence: gitglossary remote-tracking branch: "A ref that is used to follow changes from another repository... A remote-tracking branch should not contain direct modifications or have local commits made to it." But git-branch: "Use -r together with -d to delete remote-tracking branches" - a purely local command also changes these names, so "updated only by commands that contact the remote" is too absolute. Execution: `git push -q origin main` moved origin/main to the pushed commit.

claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `origin/main` is a remote-tracking name your own repository keeps as its record of where the remote's `main` stood at the last exchange; commands such as fetch, pull, push and clone update it, nothing updates it in the background, and you do not commit on it.

issues.text: The captured output and the prose explaining it come from Git 2.54.0 (lab box, `docker exec donhang-lab git --version`), not the pinned Git 2.46 (versions.yaml git: "2.46"). Behaviour differs exactly here: with Git 2.46.0 the same build-history.sh leaves no origin/HEAD after `git remote add` + `git fetch`; with 2.54.0 fetch creates refs/remotes/origin/HEAD. The lesson meanwhile names "Git 2.46" for the manual it cites, so the reader is told one version and shown another. lab/Dockerfile installs `git` from apk unpinned.
issues.quote: `origin/HEAD` is the name that records which branch that second repository starts on
issues.fix: In the lesson: replace the clause with "`origin/HEAD` names the branch that second repository starts on; the Git in the lab box records it when it fetches." and apply claim 21 suggested_text. Outside the lesson (owner decision): pin the lab box Git to the versions.yaml key, or raise versions.yaml git to the lab box version and re-review every lesson with versions_used: [git].
